summary: Applying SMOTE oversampling to the training data changed the minority-class (>50K) F1 score from 0.6816 (no resampling) to 0.6769 (SMOTE), a difference of -0.0047, which is not more than the 0.02 threshold. SMOTE decreased recall (0.6201 -> 0.6441) while decreasing precision (0.7566 -> 0.7131).
primary_metric_name: F1 difference (SMOTE - no resampling), minority class '>50K'
direction: SMOTE does not meaningfully change F1 (worsens it by 0.0047)
methodological_choices: Missing values ('?') in workclass/occupation/native-country imputed with a dedicated 'Missing' category rather than dropped or mode-imputed, to preserve all 48842 rows. All categorical features ordinal-encoded (integer codes) rather than one-hot encoded, since RandomForestClassifier() handles arbitrary integer splits and this keeps feature count low. Single stratified 75/25 train/test split (random_state=42) rather than k-fold CV, for computational simplicity and because the dataset is large enough for a stable holdout estimate. SMOTE (imblearn, default k_neighbors=5) applied only to the training set (test set left at its natural ~24%/76% imbalance) to avoid data leakage. RandomForestClassifier used with library defaults (n_estimators=100, no class_weight, no max_depth limit) in both arms except random_state=42 for reproducibility, as specified by the research question. F1, precision, and recall computed with '>50K' as the positive/minority class.
